summary: Local current-schema rules hardened and regression-tested. This conservative rollout score reflects the conditional major legacy-permission risk until trusted migration is verified; it is not a claim that live data contains unmigrated columns. Production rules, data and IAM were not inspected or deployed.

findings.issue: A column could be marked signed by referencing an existing cell event, without appending a matching sign-off. Reproduced as an unexpected HTTP 200 before the fix.
findings.recommendation: Implemented same-commit fresh immutable sign-off validation of column, author, access, revision and server timestamp.

findings.issue: Envelope writes checked the granting admin rather than the target membership, allowing delivery to absent/inactive users. Reproduced before the fix.
findings.recommendation: Implemented active recipient validation with getAfter, preserving atomic approval plus grant and admin initialization.

findings.issue: A tied editor could append a different UID to highestEditorUids. Reproduced before the fix.
findings.recommendation: Only the current editor UID may be added; duplicates are rejected. Legitimate equal-level editors remain supported.

findings.issue: Chart starts accepted negative times and unbounded session strings. Membership authorization did not check UID binding, supported role or valid access range.
findings.recommendation: Added nonnegative time, bounded session/UID/revision/index checks and shared identity/role/access membership validation.

findings.issue: For legacy columns without cellAccessLevels, the existing compatibility path cannot enforce historical encrypted per-cell permissions on the server. The client reconstructs history, but a modified client can bypass client checks. Whether such columns exist in production was not investigated.
findings.recommendation: Verify and, if needed, run the trusted migration in docs/cell-access-rollout.md before rollout. This pass preserves legacy functionality rather than silently locking those records. Migration requires authorized administrator access and the organization key for encrypted graph history.

optimization: Centralized membership identity, status, role and access validation; authenticate before membership reads.
Removed the redundant admin-or-clinician read branch because admins are supported clinical members.
Read the prior sign-off once in a helper invoked only for already signed columns; unsigned columns do not read a nonexistent prior event.
Removed an unused observation validator and unused correction arguments. Existing Firestore document-read caching means these simplifications are not a measured billing reduction.
compatibility: No new persistent fields, query filters, indexes or client changes required for the current schema.

Verified membership joining, approval, key initialization and rotation, private backup ownership, collection-group queries, roster access, archive/unarchive, saved observations, corrections and sign-off hierarchy.
Owner recovery reads for encrypted key backups remain available after membership deactivation; other users and admins cannot read them.
Clinical reads remain organization-wide. Ward/patient assignment restrictions were not introduced.
Rules validate ciphertext envelopes and authorization metadata, not encrypted clinical values or cryptographic correctness.
Legacy records with missing name fields remain supported by existing member update validators; malformed UID/role/access authority is rejected.

verification.before: 18 existing emulator test groups passed; all four new attack groups failed because prohibited writes returned HTTP 200.
verification.after: 25 emulator groups passed, 0 failures; includes valid workflow tests and malicious identity/schema/type/size writes.
verification.client_tests: 189 previously passing browser tests remain passing; Gradle reused their unchanged up-to-date results.
verification.compilation: JS and Wasm Kotlin targets successful (unchanged client outputs reused).
